pattern.title: Averages
pattern.description: Mean, weighted mean and change-in-average problems.

questions.questionText: What is the average of the numbers 52, 13, 29, 31, 30?
questions.explanation: Sum = 155. Number of values = 5. Average = 155/5 = 31.
questions.shortcut: Average = sum of values / number of values.

questions.questionText: What is the average of the numbers 61, 101, 77, 17?
questions.explanation: Sum = 256. Number of values = 4. Average = 256/4 = 64.
questions.shortcut: Average = sum of values / number of values.

questions.questionText: What is the average of the numbers 34, 45, 57, 97, 71, 56?
questions.explanation: Sum = 360. Number of values = 6. Average = 360/6 = 60.
questions.shortcut: Average = sum of values / number of values.

questions.questionText: What is the average of the numbers 25, 133, 51, 80, 21?
questions.explanation: Sum = 310. Number of values = 5. Average = 310/5 = 62.
questions.shortcut: Average = sum of values / number of values.

questions.questionText: The average of 7 consecutive odd numbers is 39. What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: The middle number is 39. Consecutive odd numbers differ by 2, so the smallest = 39 - 2 x 3 = 33.
questions.shortcut: Smallest = average - (n - 1) = 39 - 6.

questions.questionText: The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 75. What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: The middle number is 75. Consecutive odd numbers differ by 2, so the smallest = 75 - 2 x 2 = 71.
questions.shortcut: Smallest = average - (n - 1) = 75 - 4.

questions.questionText: The average of 7 consecutive even numbers is 32. What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: The middle number is 32. Consecutive even numbers differ by 2, so the smallest = 32 - 2 x 3 = 26.
questions.shortcut: Smallest = average - (n - 1) = 32 - 6.

questions.questionText: The average of 7 consecutive even numbers is 36. What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: The middle number is 36. Consecutive even numbers differ by 2, so the smallest = 36 - 2 x 3 = 30.
questions.shortcut: Smallest = average - (n - 1) = 36 - 6.

questions.questionText: The average of 9 consecutive integers is 70. What is the largest of these integers?
questions.explanation: For an odd count of consecutive integers the average is the middle number. Middle = 70, so the largest = 70 + 4 = 74.
questions.shortcut: Middle term = average; go 4 steps up for the largest.

questions.questionText: The average of 9 consecutive integers is 34. What is the largest of these integers?
questions.explanation: For an odd count of consecutive integers the average is the middle number. Middle = 34, so the largest = 34 + 4 = 38.
questions.shortcut: Middle term = average; go 4 steps up for the largest.

questions.questionText: The average of three numbers is 12. The numbers are in the ratio 2:3:7. What is the largest number?
questions.shortcut: Total = n x average; split the total in the given ratio.

questions.questionText: The average of three numbers is 16. The numbers are in the ratio 3:4:5. What is the largest number?
questions.shortcut: Total = n x average; split the total in the given ratio.

questions.questionText: In a class, 40 boys have an average of 56 marks and 60 girls have an average of 66 marks. What is the average of the whole class?
questions.explanation: Total marks = 40 x 56 + 60 x 66 = 6200. Students = 100. Average = 62.
questions.shortcut: Weighted average: add the totals, then divide by the total head count.

questions.questionText: In a class, 25 boys have an average of 57 marks and 25 girls have an average of 70 marks. What is the average of the whole class?
questions.explanation: Total marks = 25 x 57 + 25 x 70 = 3175. Students = 50. Average = 63.5.
questions.shortcut: Weighted average: add the totals, then divide by the total head count.

questions.questionText: In a class, 12 boys have an average of 60 marks and 18 girls have an average of 50 marks. What is the average of the whole class?
questions.explanation: Total marks = 12 x 60 + 18 x 50 = 1620. Students = 30. Average = 54.
questions.shortcut: Weighted average: add the totals, then divide by the total head count.

questions.questionText: In a class, 25 boys have an average of 88 marks and 25 girls have an average of 51 marks. What is the average of the whole class?
questions.explanation: Total marks = 25 x 88 + 25 x 51 = 3475. Students = 50. Average = 69.5.
questions.shortcut: Weighted average: add the totals, then divide by the total head count.

questions.questionText: The average marks of a class of 30 students is 66. The boys' average is 69 and the girls' average is 64. How many boys are there?
questions.shortcut: Alligation: boys : girls = (class avg - girls avg) : (boys avg - class avg).

questions.questionText: The average marks of a class of 40 students is 62. The boys' average is 77 and the girls' average is 53. How many boys are there?
questions.shortcut: Alligation: boys : girls = (class avg - girls avg) : (boys avg - class avg).

questions.questionText: The average marks of a class of 50 students is 71. The boys' average is 80 and the girls' average is 50. How many boys are there?
questions.shortcut: Alligation: boys : girls = (class avg - girls avg) : (boys avg - class avg).

questions.questionText: The average marks of a class of 40 students is 65. The boys' average is 80 and the girls' average is 56. How many boys are there?
questions.shortcut: Alligation: boys : girls = (class avg - girls avg) : (boys avg - class avg).

questions.questionText: The average of 20 numbers is 78. When two of the numbers, 29 and 82, are removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.shortcut: Subtract the removed values from the total; divide by the remaining count.

questions.questionText: The average of 20 numbers is 32. When two of the numbers, 20 and 26, are removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: Total = 20 x 32 = 640. After removal: 640 - 20 - 26 = 594. Average = 594/18 = 33.
questions.shortcut: Subtract the removed values from the total; divide by the remaining count.

questions.questionText: The average of 20 numbers is 41. When two of the numbers, 38 and 62, are removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: Total = 20 x 41 = 820. After removal: 820 - 38 - 62 = 720. Average = 720/18 = 40.
questions.shortcut: Subtract the removed values from the total; divide by the remaining count.

questions.questionText: The average marks of 24 students in a test is 84. A new student scoring 34 marks joins them. What is the new average?
questions.explanation: Old total = 24 x 84 = 2016. New total = 2016 + 34 = 2050. New average = 2050/25 = 82.
questions.shortcut: Rebuild the total (n x average), add the new value, divide by the new count.

questions.questionText: The average marks of 24 students in a test is 70. A new student scoring 45 marks joins them. What is the new average?
questions.explanation: Old total = 24 x 70 = 1680. New total = 1680 + 45 = 1725. New average = 1725/25 = 69.
questions.shortcut: Rebuild the total (n x average), add the new value, divide by the new count.

questions.questionText: The average marks of 19 students in a test is 56. A new student scoring 76 marks joins them. What is the new average?
questions.explanation: Old total = 19 x 56 = 1064. New total = 1064 + 76 = 1140. New average = 1140/20 = 57.
questions.shortcut: Rebuild the total (n x average), add the new value, divide by the new count.

questions.questionText: The average marks of 11 students in a test is 63. A new student scoring 87 marks joins them. What is the new average?
questions.explanation: Old total = 11 x 63 = 693. New total = 693 + 87 = 780. New average = 780/12 = 65.
questions.shortcut: Rebuild the total (n x average), add the new value, divide by the new count.

questions.questionText: The average weight of 10 persons increases by 1 kg when a person weighing 40 kg is replaced by a new person. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Change in total = 10 x 1 = 10 kg. New person = 40 + 10 = 50 kg.
questions.shortcut: Change in total = number of persons x change in average; apply it to the replaced value.

questions.questionText: The average weight of 15 persons decreases by 1.5 kg when a person weighing 52 kg is replaced by a new person. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Change in total = 15 x 1.5 = 22.5 kg. New person = 52 - 22.5 = 29.5 kg.
questions.shortcut: Change in total = number of persons x change in average; apply it to the replaced value.

questions.questionText: The average weight of 20 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a person weighing 63 kg is replaced by a new person. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Change in total = 20 x 2.5 = 50 kg. New person = 63 + 50 = 113 kg.
questions.shortcut: Change in total = number of persons x change in average; apply it to the replaced value.

questions.questionText: The average weight of 5 persons increases by 1 kg when a person weighing 65 kg is replaced by a new person. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Change in total = 5 x 1 = 5 kg. New person = 65 + 5 = 70 kg.

questions.questionText: The average weight of 5 persons increases by 2 kg when a person weighing 71 kg is replaced by a new person. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Change in total = 5 x 2 = 10 kg. New person = 71 + 10 = 81 kg.

questions.questionText: The average weight of 20 persons increases by 4 kg when a person weighing 72 kg is replaced by a new person. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Change in total = 20 x 4 = 80 kg. New person = 72 + 80 = 152 kg.

questions.questionText: The average of 10 numbers was calculated as 57. It was later found that the number 59 had been wrongly read as 14. What is the correct average?
questions.explanation: Wrong total = 10 x 57 = 570. Correct total = 570 - 14 + 59 = 615. Correct average = 615/10 = 61.5.
questions.shortcut: Correct average = old average + (right - wrong)/10.

questions.questionText: The average of 10 numbers was calculated as 69. It was later found that the number 15 had been wrongly read as 10. What is the correct average?
questions.explanation: Wrong total = 10 x 69 = 690. Correct total = 690 - 10 + 15 = 695. Correct average = 695/10 = 69.5.
questions.shortcut: Correct average = old average + (right - wrong)/10.

questions.questionText: The average age of 39 students is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average increases by 2 year(s). What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation: New average = 16. Total with teacher = 40 x 16 = 640. Students' total = 39 x 14 = 546. Teacher = 94 years.
questions.shortcut: Teacher's age = old average + (n + 1) x rise = 14 + 40 x 2.

questions.questionText: The average age of 29 students is 12 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average increases by 2 year(s). What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation: New average = 14. Total with teacher = 30 x 14 = 420. Students' total = 29 x 12 = 348. Teacher = 72 years.

questions.questionText: The average age of a family of 6 members is 36 years and the youngest member is 11 years old. What was the average age of the family at the time of the birth of the youngest member?
questions.explanation: Sum of ages of the other 5 members now = 216 - 11 = 205. At the birth, each was 11 years younger: 205 - 55 = 150. Average = 150/5 = 30 years.
questions.shortcut: Only 5 members existed at that time, and each was 11 years younger.

questions.explanation: Sum of ages of the other 4 members now = 155 - 11 = 144. At the birth, each was 11 years younger: 144 - 44 = 100. Average = 100/4 = 25 years.

questions.explanation: Average of the first n natural numbers = (n + 1)/2 = (20 + 1)/2 = 10.5.

questions.questionText: What is the average of the first 40 even natural numbers?

questions.questionText: What is the average of the first 25 even natural numbers?

questions.questionText: What is the average of all odd numbers between 34 and 74?
questions.explanation: The odd numbers run from 35 to 73. They are evenly spaced, so average = (35 + 73)/2 = 54.
questions.shortcut: For an evenly spaced list: average = (first + last)/2.

questions.questionText: What is the average of all even numbers between 18 and 68?
questions.explanation: The even numbers run from 20 to 66. They are evenly spaced, so average = (20 + 66)/2 = 43.

questions.questionText: What is the average of all even numbers between 58 and 98?

questions.questionText: What is the average of all multiples of 4 from 4 to 80?
questions.explanation: The multiples are 4 x 1 up to 4 x 20. Average = 4 x (1 + 20)/2 = 42.
questions.shortcut: Average of multiples = k x (first + last index)/2.

questions.questionText: What is the average of all multiples of 4 from 4 to 48?

questions.questionText: The average of the first n multiples of 4 is 52. What is the value of n?
questions.explanation: Average of the first n multiples of 4 = 4(n + 1)/2 = 52, so n + 1 = 26 and n = 25.
questions.shortcut: n = 2 x average / 4 - 1.

questions.questionText: The average of the first n multiples of 8 is 56. What is the value of n?

questions.questionText: The average of the first n multiples of 9 is 54. What is the value of n?

questions.shortcut: n = 2 x average / 9 - 1.

questions.questionText: The average of 8 numbers is 47. The average of 6 of them is 42. What is the average of the remaining 2 numbers?
questions.explanation: Total = 376. Total of the 6 numbers = 252. Remaining total = 124. Average = 124/2 = 62.
questions.shortcut: Subtract the known group total from the overall total, then divide by the leftover count.

questions.questionText: The average of 5 numbers is 26. The average of 2 of them is 29. What is the average of the remaining 3 numbers?

questions.questionText: The average of 9 numbers is 49. The average of the first 5 numbers is 58 and the average of the last 5 numbers is 33. What is the middle number?
questions.explanation: First 5 total = 290, last 5 total = 165. Their sum counts the middle number twice: 455 - 9 x 49 = 14.
questions.shortcut: Middle number = (sum of the two overlapping group totals) - (total of all).
